ei.title: A Journey From War to the Olympics
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
When Yusra Mardini was a young girl growing up in Damascus, Syria, her life centered around swimming. Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. It was clear that she had a special talent, and she fell in love with the sport. She enjoyed watching Olympic swimming events with her father, which led her to dream about competing in the Olympics. She got the chance to represent Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true.

However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war. If they reached Europe, the rest of the family would follow. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to pursue her dream and live without fear.

In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather rapidly grew worse. The heavy boat began to sink, and the panicked, desperate passengers had no choice but to throw their possessions into the sea. Yusra felt heartbroken as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves. However, she had no time to reflect. She had to take action immediately in order to save herself and the other passengers. She jumped into the water along with Sara and two others, and the four of them guided the drifting boat. They swam for three and a half hours until they arrived safely with all the other passengers on the shore of a Greek island.

Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land.

She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.

Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with pity instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.

At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was determined to pour everything she had into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter. In one interview, when a reporter asked if she could make a statement, she remarked, "I want everyone to stay strong for their goals in life, because if you have your goals in front of your eyes, you will do everything you can; and I think even if I fail, I will try again. ... I want to show everybody that it's hard to arrive at your dreams, but it's not impossible. You can do it; everyone can do it."

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One (A)[fortunate / fateful] day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was (B)[horrifying / reassuring] enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to (C)[flee / settle in] Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ (A) fateful(운명적인): 폭탄이 떨어진 불길한 날 ← 정답
❌ fortunate(운이 좋은): 폭탄 사건에 부적절
✅ (B) horrifying(끔찍한): 경각심을 줄 정도로 끔찍한 사건
❌ reassuring(안심시키는): 문맥상 정반대
✅ (C) flee(도망치다): 전쟁을 피해 시리아를 떠나기로 결심
❌ settle in(정착하다): 떠나기로 했으므로 부적절
det.tip: fateful = 운명을 바꿀 만한. horrifying = 끔찍한. flee = 도망치다.

questions.passage: She got the chance to (A)[represent / betray] Syria in an international swimming championship, and it seemed like her Olympic dream might someday come true. However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this (B)[harmony / chaos], she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became (C)[enjoyable / dangerous].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① betray(배신하다): 시리아를 대표할 기회이므로 부적절
❌ ② harmony(조화): 내전 상황이므로 혼란이 맞음
❌ ③ enjoyable(즐거운): 전쟁 중이므로 위험한이 적절
✅ ④ represent — chaos — dangerous: 원문과 일치 ← 정답
det.tip: represent = 대표하다. chaos = 혼란. 전쟁 맥락에서 부정적 어휘가 적절.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her (A)[outstanding / mediocre] talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and (B)[indifferent / persistent] in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would (C)[fall apart / pay off] one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① indifferent(무관심한): 노력 추구와 모순
❌ ② mediocre(평범한): 즉시 인정한 재능이므로 부적절
✅ ③ outstanding — persistent — pay off: 원문과 일치 ← 정답
❌ ④ fall apart(무너지다): 희망의 문맥과 모순
det.tip: outstanding = 뛰어난. persistent = 끈기 있는. pay off = (노력이) 성과를 내다.

questions.passage: Next, Yusra and Sara had to travel through Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, and Austria. They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how ①<u>exhausted</u> they were, they kept moving. At the end of this ②<u>relaxing</u> 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a ③<u>refugee</u> center in Berlin. Despite all the ④<u>hardships</u> and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② relaxing → overwhelming: 25일간의 여정은 '압도적인/벅찬' 것이지 '편안한' 것이 아님
det.analysis:
✅ ① exhausted(지친): 원문 일치
❌ ② relaxing(편안한) → overwhelming(압도적인): 고난의 여정이므로 부적절 ← 정답
✅ ③ refugee(난민): 원문 일치
✅ ④ hardships(고난): 원문 일치
det.tip: overwhelming = 압도적인, 벅찬. relaxing = 편안한. 정반대 의미.

questions.passage:
Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great ①<u>opportunity</u>, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might view her with ②<u>pity</u> instead of seeing her as a serious ③<u>amateur</u>. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ amateur → athlete: 진지한 '운동선수'로 보이고 싶은 것이지 '아마추어'가 아님
det.analysis:
✅ ① opportunity(기회): 원문 일치
✅ ② pity(동정): 원문 일치
❌ ③ amateur(아마추어) → athlete(운동선수): serious athlete가 원문 ← 정답
✅ ④ inspire(영감을 주다): 원문 일치
det.tip: athlete = 운동선수. amateur = 아마추어. serious athlete = 진지한 운동선수.

questions.passage: In August, 2015, the sisters began their dangerous journey by making their way to their first destination, Türkiye. There, along with 18 other people, including children and babies, they boarded a tiny boat designed for seven passengers. They were heading across the sea towards Greece when disaster struck. The boat's engine failed in the middle of the open sea, and the weather ①<u>rapidly</u> grew worse. Yusra felt ④<u>relieved</u> as she watched people's treasured belongings disappear under the waves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ relieved → heartbroken: 소중한 물건이 파도 아래 사라지는 것을 보고 '안도'가 아닌 '비통함'
det.analysis:
✅ ① rapidly(빠르게): 원문 일치
✅ ② desperate(절박한): 원문 일치
✅ ③ possessions(소유물): 원문 일치
❌ ④ relieved(안도하는) → heartbroken(비통한): 소중한 물건이 사라지는 슬픈 상황 ← 정답
det.tip: heartbroken = 비통한. relieved = 안도하는. 정반대 감정.

questions.passage: Her father was a former professional swimmer, and she started learning how to swim from a young age. When she was nine years old, she was already faster than many older swimmers. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① talent(재능): 9살에 나이 든 선수보다 빠름 → 재능 ← 정답
❌ ② burden(짐): 수영을 사랑했으므로 짐이 아님
❌ ③ routine(일상): special과 어울리지 않음
❌ ④ conflict(갈등): 사랑에 빠진 맥락과 무관
det.tip: talent = 재능. It was clear that she had a special talent.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full __________. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: potential(잠재력): 코치가 '최대 잠재력'에 도달하도록 도울 수 있는
det.analysis:
✅ ② potential(잠재력): reach her full potential = 잠재력 발휘 ← 정답
❌ ① schedule(일정): 코치를 찾는 맥락에 부적절
❌ ③ isolation(고립): 도움 받는 맥락과 무관
❌ ④ confusion(혼란): 훈련 맥락과 무관
det.tip: reach one's full potential = 최대 잠재력을 발휘하다.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a __________ for Yusra and her sister Sara.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: wake-up call(경각심을 일깨우는 사건): 수영장에 폭탄이 떨어진 사건이 경각심을 일깨운 계기
det.analysis:
✅ ③ wake-up call(경각심): 폭탄 사건 후 더 이상 머물 수 없다고 깨달음 ← 정답
❌ ① celebration(축하): 폭탄 사건과 정반대
❌ ② coincidence(우연의 일치): 사건의 심각성과 무관
❌ ④ compliment(칭찬): 문맥과 전혀 무관
det.tip: wake-up call = 경종, 경각심을 일깨우는 사건.

questions.passage: However, Yusra had no idea that her life would soon be turned upside down by the horrors of the Syrian civil war, which had broken out in 2011. Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she <u>clung</u> to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became dangerous. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 clung의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① held on to(붙잡다): clung to = 매달리다 ← 정답
❌ ② let go of(놓아주다): 반의어
❌ ③ forgot about(잊다): 꿈에 매달린 것이므로 반대
❌ ④ argued about(논쟁하다): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: cling - clung - clung: ~에 매달리다. clung to her dream = 꿈을 놓지 않았다.

questions.passage: They walked great distances, and even though they caught rides in small cars and crowded buses from time to time, they had to cross every border on foot. No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this <u>overwhelming</u> 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and adversities she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her. In fact, it was the only thing she could do to feel at home in this foreign land.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 overwhelming의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ overpowering(압도적인): overwhelming과 동의어 ← 정답
❌ ① pleasant(즐거운): 고난의 여정이므로 반대
❌ ② brief(짧은): 25일간이므로 짧지 않음
❌ ④ ordinary(평범한): 극한 여정이므로 부적절
det.tip: overwhelming = 압도적인, 벅찬. overpowering = 압도하는.

questions.passage: One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara. They realized that they could no longer stay in their home country, and they made up their minds to flee Syria and go to Germany to avoid the war. If they reached Europe, the rest of the family would follow. The decision was not an easy one, but Yusra knew that it was her only option if she wanted to <u>pursue</u> her dream and live without fear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 pursue의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② chase(추구하다): pursue와 동의어 ← 정답
❌ ① abandon(포기하다): 반의어
❌ ③ avoid(피하다): 꿈을 추구하므로 반대
❌ ④ delay(미루다): 적극 추구이므로 부적절
det.tip: pursue = 추구하다, 쫓다. pursue one's dream = 꿈을 추구하다.

questions.passage: Over the next few years, normal activities like going to school became risky. Through all of this chaos, she clung to her dream and kept swimming. However, even this became <u>dangerous</u>. One fateful day, a bomb fell in the pool where she was training. Although it did not explode, this incident was horrifying enough to be a wake-up call for Yusra and her sister Sara.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 dangerous의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ safe(안전한): dangerous의 반의어 ← 정답
❌ ① risky(위험한): dangerous와 유의어
❌ ② harmful(해로운): dangerous와 유사
❌ ④ threatening(위협적인): dangerous와 유사
det.tip: dangerous ↔ safe. 위험한 ↔ 안전한.

questions.passage: She decided to take up training again, and she started looking for a coach in Berlin who could help her reach her full potential. She eventually met Sven Spannekrebs at a swimming club near the refugee center and asked if he could be her coach. When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay focused and <u>persistent</u> in her efforts to pursue excellence. Following his instructions, Yusra trained hard day and night, hoping her efforts would pay off one day.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 persistent의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② fickle(변덕스러운): persistent의 반의어. 쉽게 포기하는 성향 ← 정답
❌ ① determined(단호한): persistent와 유사(의지)
❌ ③ rapid(빠른): 의미축이 다름(속도)
❌ ④ dedicated(헌신적인): persistent와 유사(노력)
det.tip: persistent = 끈기 있는. fickle = 변덕스러운. 꾸준함 ↔ 변덕.

questions.passage:
(A) After years of effort, Yusra finally had a chance to <u>make</u> her dream a reality at the Olympic Games.

(B) When the reporter asked if she could <u>make</u> a statement, Yusra eagerly agreed and shared her inspiring message.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 make의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) make her dream a reality = 이루다 / (B) make a statement = 발표하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① 이루다 — 발표하다: (A) 꿈을 실현하다, (B) 성명을 발표하다 ← 정답
❌ ② 만들다 — 이루다: (A)는 '실현하다'이고 (B)는 '발표하다'
❌ ③ 시키다 — 결정하다: 두 문맥 모두 부적절
❌ ④ 구성하다 — 벌다: 두 문맥 모두 부적절
det.tip: make a dream a reality = 꿈을 이루다. make a statement = 성명을 발표하다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster"

det.korean: refugee(난민): 전쟁이나 박해를 피해 고국을 떠나도록 강요당한 사람
det.analysis:
✅ ④ refugee(난민): 전쟁/박해로 강제 이주한 사람 ← 정답
❌ ① volunteer(자원봉사자): 자발적 활동
❌ ② immigrant(이민자): 자발적 이주 (강제 아님)
❌ ③ tourist(관광객): 여행 목적
det.tip: refugee = 난민. forced to leave = 강제로 떠나야 하는. 핵심 단서: escape war.

questions.passage: When he saw her swim, he immediately recognized her outstanding talent and agreed to do so. Sven helped Yusra stay __________ (focus) and persistent in her efforts to pursue excellence.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: ✅ focused: stay + 형용사보어. focus(동사) → focused(과거분사/형용사) 변환.
det.tip: stay + 형용사: focused(집중된). focus → focused(과거분사의 형용사적 용법).

questions.passage: No matter how exhausted they were, they kept moving. At the end of this overwhelming 25-day journey, they finally made it to Germany and settled at a refugee center in Berlin. Despite all the hardships and __________ (adverse) she underwent, Yusra's passion for swimming never left her.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: ✅ adversities: adverse(형용사) → adversity(명사) → adversities(복수). and로 연결된 hardships와 병렬 구조이므로 복수 명사 필요.
det.tip: adverse(형용사: 불리한) → adversity(명사: 역경) → adversities(복수). 병렬 구조(hardships and __)에서 복수 명사.

questions.passage: Yusra soon received a chance to make her dream a reality when she was invited to join the first ever refugee team at the 2016 Summer Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro. Although it seemed like a great opportunity, Yusra was hesitant. If she joined the refugee team, she thought, people might __________ instead of seeing her as a serious athlete. She almost turned down the invitation, but she decided to accept it after she realized that she could inspire hope in millions of other refugees facing similar challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사람들이 그녀를 동정의 시선으로 볼(view her with pity) 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ② view her with pity(동정으로 보다): 원문 'people might view her with pity' 일치 ← 정답
❌ ① admire her courage(용기를 존경): 원문의 우려와 반대
❌ ③ celebrate her success(성공 축하): 아직 경기 전
❌ ④ ignore her completely(완전 무시): 문맥에 무시 언급 없음
det.tip: view her with pity = 동정의 눈으로 보다. instead of와 대조 관계.

questions.passage: At the Games, Yusra competed in both the 100-meter butterfly and the 100-meter freestyle events. When she stepped onto the starting blocks, she was determined to __________ into the competition. She came in 41st out of 45 competitors in the butterfly and 45th out of 46 in the freestyle event. Even though she left the Olympics without a medal, she was proud to have made history alongside her teammates. The time on the scoreboard did not matter.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경기에 가진 모든 것을 쏟아붓겠다(pour everything she had)는 결심
det.analysis:
✅ ④ pour everything she had(모든 것을 쏟아붓다): 원문 일치. determined to pour ← 정답
❌ ① hold back her energy(에너지를 아끼다): determined와 모순
❌ ② make a quick escape(빨리 도망치다): 경기 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ take a careful approach(신중하게 접근): 모든 것을 쏟겠다는 결심과 불일치
det.tip: pour everything into = ~에 모든 것을 쏟다. determined = 결심한.
